resources.string: Apps, sites, DPI bypass and exits in one place
Decide what goes through the VPN, what goes around it and what gets a special exit. Four tabs, one question each.
An exit is where traffic leaves: the VPN, directly, DPI bypass, Telegram over WebSocket or any server. Here you build groups of exits and chain servers.
The basic switch: everything, only the ticked apps, or everything except them.
Which sites and addresses use the VPN
Same idea, but by domain or IP range instead of by app.
A separate exit for an app
For example: send one app through a chosen server or through DPI bypass while the rest follows the mode above.
Rules for sites, IPs, countries and ports
What matches → which exit. Rules are checked top to bottom; the first match wins.
NOT inverts the condition. Rules with the same label are joined by AND (for example port 443 AND a country).
Auto — the fastest live exit, with failover
Word inside a domain, e.g. google
Country code or set, e.g. ru
Or type your own (ciadpi arguments, for experts)
When Telegram will not load even with DPI bypass
Telegram traffic goes to its servers over a TLS WebSocket (kws*.web.telegram.org) instead of plain TCP, which providers throttle. Works without a server of your own. Android and desktop.
